flows.title: A home for the whole family
flows.purpose: See who you’re thinking of, what’s coming up, and where a little help is needed.
flows.today: The current dashboard brings together the next occasion, gift counts, an idea inbox, and recent activity.
options: A celebration and familiar faces lead; the next useful action follows.
Shared tasks and buying ownership lead in a compact, tactile board.
People, celebrations, and ideas become places on a little illustrated map.
flows.reason: It says “people we care about” before it asks anyone to manage tasks. Keep the task summary within easy reach.
steps: A familiar celebration anchors the page.
Their avatar carries into the profile header.
flows.motion: A keeps the person’s avatar continuous. B updates a task row in place. C follows a short path between destinations. Avoid bouncing the entire page.

flows.title: Remember what makes them smile
flows.purpose: Keep relationships, preferences, useful notes, gift ideas, and past gifts together.
flows.today: The standalone profile has information, lists, and history tabs. Opening a person’s card adds a richer overlay with budgets, advanced preferences, linked records, comments, and history.
options: Interests sit beside gift ideas, with preferences and past gifts close by.
Group this person’s gifts by who still needs to buy and what is already in hand.
Small observations become a timeline that can spark a gift idea.
flows.reason: Remembering a person and choosing for them belong together. It gives the app a warmer purpose while preserving the deeper preferences.
steps: Tea, gardening, and mysteries stay in view.
The gift grows into a focused detail sheet.
Returning restores the same person and tab.
flows.motion: A expands the chosen gift into a sheet. B carries a gift row between stages. C gently reveals a note’s gift action. Restore scroll position and keyboard focus.

flows.title: Make a plan with room for joy
flows.purpose: Bring recipients, lists, budgets, and shared buying progress into one celebration.
flows.today: The current occasion page links recipients and lists with budget controls further down. Its phone layout currently overflows horizontally; saving a budget returned a server error even though the value later appeared.
options: A celebration scene and people’s readiness lead the plan.
Bought, set aside, and available stay visible beside the recipient ledger.
Plan by what happens now, before the gathering, and on the day.
flows.reason: It makes financial room and remaining work easy to compare. Keep the celebration illustration small enough that the plan comes first.
steps: See bought, committed, and remaining together.
Their gifts open without losing the occasion.
The budget bar and gift stage settle together.
flows.motion: A lifts a recipient into their plan. B animates only the changed budget segment and ledger row. C advances the timeline marker. Always show the final amount as text.

flows.title: From a lovely idea to “I’ve got it”
flows.purpose: Capture a gift, connect it to someone and an occasion, choose a buyer, and track it through buying.
flows.today: The current list board already has idea, selected, purchased, and received stages. Catalog gifts and list items carry separate state; the assignments view is a separate screen.
options: A focused gift sheet makes its recipient, buyer, and next action unmistakable.
Keep unclaimed, buying, and bought gifts together so the family can coordinate.
A checklist records the gift’s journey with buyer and recipient clearly separated.
flows.reason: Who is buying what is the coordination problem this app can solve best. Use a focused sheet like A when someone claims or buys a gift.
steps: The gift appears under “Needs a buyer”.
A named owner replaces the claim action.
The same gift moves to “Bought”, with undo.
flows.motion: A advances the gift’s stage in place. B moves one stable card between sections. C checks the next passport entry. Use a short settle, explicit status text, and a visible undo.
